scope: Reproducibility of the APPLIED-arm hard count and attribution of the live-vs-census delta only. This review does not rule on whether rubric-literal HF-02 applies to ledger class_ids arrays, and it does not adopt, retire or edit any artifact.
method: Read-only. Frozen detector bytes loaded from the hash-verified worker-073 pin a8c04fc3, applied to (i) the worker-031 pin of the r3 snapshot f344ed2a and (ii) the live map; findings compared by claim-index multiset and by finding text. Result: artifacts/worker-061/classsep_census_reconcile_10/probe_output.json.

findings.finding: The r3 census APPLIED arm is exactly reproducible at map f344ed2a (383 claims) with detector a8c04fc3: 19 hard findings over 14 unique claim indices {36,94,96,97,101,112,144,152,180,192,276,306,327,336}, multiplicity 192x3, 276x3, 112x2, rest x1. Recorded finding strings are exact 180/200-char prefixes of the measured strings.

The live count of 23 is the same 19 findings plus exactly 4 net-new findings on claims appended after the r3 snapshot (indices 393, 395, 406, 410); no r3 hit disappeared and no common index changed multiplicity. Across the two live reads made during this run the map grew 543 -> 579 claims while the count stayed 23, i.e. the extra 36 claims added no further hits. There is no detector instability and no claim mutation on this axis.

corpus_b_live.APPLIED.labeled_claims is a label-corpus membership list, not the flagged-index set: it contains 127 and 187 (which do not fire at the frozen bytes) and omits 327 and 336 (which do fire as unlabeled DETECTOR_SELF). The 19-count and the record's claims_flagged=14 are both correct; only a reader who treats labeled_claims as the hit list would be misled. Recommendation for the 02:30 review: reconstruct the hit set as labeled_detail UNION unlabeled.

The record truncates finding strings at 180 chars (17 labeled) and 200 chars (2 unlabeled). A naive string-equality diff against a fresh detector run reports a false mismatch; the correct comparison is recorded-prefix against measured string.

Of the 196 claims appended after the r3 snapshot, 68 (34.7%) match a detector-meta lexicon (class_separation/CLASSSEP/detector/census/hard fail/composite C0/C2/merge assertion), and 3 of the 4 net-new hard hits are such meta-traffic (395, 406, 410). This gives a measured rate for CF-16's unbounded-rewording-loop mechanism. Descriptive only; no detector change is proposed.

The controller checkpoint's 23 CLASSSEP entries are multiset- and text-identical to the independent live detector run at the same instant. Any future divergence between the controller count and a fresh run is map growth or detector movement, not a counting defect.

controls: 7/7 (K1 detector pin identity, K2 synthetic positive fires, K3 r3 reproduction/prefixes, K4 injection fires at new index only, K5 null split-sentence silent, K6 declared pins stable, K7 no canonical write)
